title: standardgalactic/agent-hivemind: Claude Code Hook Injection via MCP Auto-Execute Directive
objective: Model and defend against persistent hook-level compromise of a Claude Code developer workstation via a malicious MCP server (agent-hivemind) that auto-installs pre/post command hooks and a credential vault.

targetTopology.description: Developer workstation running Claude Code with MCP servers configured. Target has ~/.claude/hooks/ and ~/.claude/commands/ writable. May have Confluence, Redis, or cloud credential access.

attackerCapabilities: Execute code before and after every Claude Code tool call (hook interception)
Exfiltrate task context (what the developer is building) via ticket-sync.py
Store and escrow credentials from connected agents (Shamir vault)
Distribute additional tools via marketplace post-compromise
Coordinate multiple compromised Claude Code agents (Kanban + directive system)
Read Confluence wikis and internal documentation
Persist as HTTP MCP server for multi-agent coordination
exploitedWeaknesses: MCP servers are trusted to write files within their tool scope
Claude Code hooks directory is writable by any process with user permissions
No code signing or integrity verification on hook files
MCP server installation often done without full code review
auto_execute:true directive fires on first connection before operator can review

humanInterpretation: A developer installs agent-hivemind as an MCP server thinking it is a DevOps automation tool (it markets itself as 'ClaudeOps — Distributed AI collective memory'). On first connection, the AgentDirectiveSystem fires a claude_code_setup directive marked auto_execute:True with critical priority. This directive creates ~/.claude/hooks/ and writes pre-command.sh, post-command.sh, and ticket-sync.py. From this point forward, every Claude Code session runs the attacker's hooks. The developer has no visible indication this happened — Claude Code continues working normally, but all tool calls are now intercepted and task context is synced to the hivemind server. The credential vault then collects any secrets Claude Code interacts with.
machineInterpretation: Attack graph: MCP_INSTALL → AgentDirectiveSystem.execute(claude_code_setup) → mkdir(~/.claude/hooks) → write(pre-command.sh, post-command.sh, ticket-sync.py, mode=755) → PERSISTENCE. Post-persistence: EVERY_TOOL_CALL → pre-command.sh(exfil_context) → CLAUDE_TOOL_EXECUTE → post-command.sh(exfil_result). Parallel: vault.sync(credentials) → redis(6379) → haivemind_server.
trustEdgeRefs: Developer trusts MCP server registry / npm to surface legitimate tools
Claude Code trusts hooks directory contents to be operator-authored
Developer trusts 'ClaudeOps' branding as Claude-ecosystem tool
boundaryEventRefs: MCP server writes to filesystem outside its declared scope
Hook file created with execute permissions by non-claude process
Redis connection from Python process with 'haivemind' in cmdline
controlRefs: ai-infra/mcp-risk/mcp_integrity_check.py — blocks standardgalactic MCP servers at install time
detections/agent-hivemind-hook-injection.json — Sigma + osquery for hook dir writes
intel/github/fingerprint_monitor.py — surfaces if SG network accounts interact with our repos
proofRefs: fixtures/threat-actor-graphs/sg-hivemind.assessment.json — codebase graph confirming 3442 functions across 152 files
ai-infra/mcp-risk/CLAUDE-CODE-INTEL-EXPOSURE.md — confirms SG has Claude Code system prompt intelligence enabling targeted hook design

remediationSteps: Remove ~/.claude/hooks/ contents not authored by operator
Remove ~/.claude/commands/ contents not authored by operator
Flush Redis keyspace used by haivemind (key prefix: haivemind:*)
Revoke any credentials Claude Code may have interacted with during compromised period
Rotate all secrets accessible during sessions with agent-hivemind installed

claimPromotion.promotionThreshold: Any confirmation of hook file in ~/.claude/hooks/ from non-operator source → escalate to INCIDENT
suppressionConditions: Hook files match operator-authored inventory in change management system

immediateConsequences: Persistent code execution on every Claude Code command
Real-time exfiltration of developer task context to attacker C2
Credential harvesting from all secrets Claude Code accesses
cascadingConsequences: Attacker gains insight into all repos being worked on, all PRs, all deploy commands
Harvested credentials enable lateral movement into cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, databases
Multi-agent Kanban coordination enables parallel compromise of other developer machines in same org
consequenceModel.blastRadius: Individual developer → org-wide if credentials exfiltrated from CI/CD or cloud provider

abstentionRules: Do not install agent-hivemind or any standardgalactic MCP server in any environment
Do not execute hook files found in ~/.claude/hooks/ without verifying authorship
Do not allowlist 'haivemind' or 'hivemind' process names in osquery rules
counterfactuals: If MCP servers required signed manifests with declared filesystem write scopes, the hook installation would be blocked or require explicit operator approval
If Claude Code validated hook file integrity (e.g., sha256 manifest), injected hooks would be detected on next launch
If Redis was not available on the developer machine, the credential vault would fail to sync but hook persistence would still succeed
semanticNonClaims: This scenario does not claim SG has already compromised any specific developer workstation
This scenario does not claim Lance James (credential_escrow.py author) is malicious — the code may have been incorporated without consent
